keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Livonian Confederation and Terra Mariana pages say 'The largest ecclesiastical state was the Archbishopric of Riga (18,000 km2)'; the pages name no castle or district. A disc stands for it. Revised after review eu-14-x: the first disc (80 km round Riga, 20,485 km2) covered 8,096 km2 of the semigallians shape, which stays free to 1290; the disc now has a 70 km radius round 25.1E 57.25N, north-east of the Daugava, and Semigallia is cut away from the whole shape; with the Riga circle and Ikšķile it draws about 17,700 km2 against the infobox's 18,000 km2 (ratio 0.98). The placement is the reviewer's suggestion, not a page: no district name is on the pages opened (Kokenhusen, Lemsal, Ronneburg, Treiden are not); the disc overlaps the Turaida and Idumeja circles of the livonians dossier (Livonian to 1206 and 1208, one year of overlap in 1207) and the Order's Cliopatria-derived shapes. 1207 is the page's date for Terra Mariana ('established on 2 February 1207'), not a date for the archbishopric's land.

ledger.note: 1201: Riga is founded on the Daugava Livonians' land and becomes the bishop's seat. 'Building started in 1201. From this settlement, the city of Riga grew' (Livonians page); Albert 'forced the Livonian leaders at the mouth of the Daugava River to give him land to build a Christian settlement' (the page gives no year for the grant). The Archbishopric page puts the see at Riga in 1202. The year is the page's; the 35 km circle is the livonians dossier's, which files the matching 1201 loss.

1202: the seat moves to Riga. 'The see became the Bishopric of Riga in 1202'; Albert of Riga is bishop 1202-1229. The Riga page dates the move to the founding of Riga in 1201 ('Bishop Albert transferred the seat of the Livonian bishopric from Uexküll to Riga').

ledger.note: 1207: Terra Mariana is established ('on 2 February 1207'), with the Archbishopric of Riga as its largest ecclesiastical state (18,000 km2) and the archbishop as nominal head of Terra Mariana and of the city of Riga. The pages give no date for when the archbishopric's land was acquired and no district names; the whole disc is therefore carried at confidence 1. 'This division of medieval Livonia was created by Papal Legate William of Modena in 1228' (Terra Mariana page), between the church and the Sword Brothers. Counterpart revised after review eu-14-x: 'nobody'. The livonians dossier files its 1206 and 1208 losses to the Brothers of the Sword and no 1207 loss, the Brothers dossier no 1207 loss to the archbishop, and the pages opened name no donor for the archbishop's land beyond the Riga circle (the Livonians page has no 1206-1208 division); a donor is therefore not asserted.
1255: the Bishopric of Riga is elevated. 'It was elevated to an archbishopric in 1255.' Albert had 'failed in his aspiration to be anointed archbishop' (Riga page).

'In 1561, during the Livonian War, Terra Mariana ceased to exist'; 'the southern territories became part of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania as the Duchy of Livonia'. The Archbishopric page says the diocese 'ended in 1561' while its list gives William of Brandenburg 1539-1563; the Livonian War page says Wilhelm von Brandenburg 'was appointed as Archbishop of Riga' and was captured in the 1556 events, with no dates.

1561: Riga leaves the archbishop. The Riga page gives 1561 with the Livonian Order's end and says Riga 'for twenty years had the status of a free imperial city'; the Livonian Confederation page says Riga became a free imperial city 'the following year' after William of Brandenburg lost the territory. 1561 is used; the Livonian War page is silent on this.

notes: Ecclesiastical principality of Terra Mariana and member of the Livonian Confederation (signed at Walk on 4 December 1435, a document of church, Order, vassals and cities: an association, not territory). The pages give only the area and the capital, so the shape is a disc and the dating of the archbishopric's land is page-silent; this is the thinnest of the Livonian church dossiers and the first to improve if a source with district names (Kokenhusen, Lemsal, Ronneburg, Salis, Treiden are not on the pages opened) is found. The Riga page infobox gives 1201-1561 for the archbishopric; the Archbishopric page gives the see of Riga in 1202. Tālava is divided between the Archbishopric and the Order in 1224 and the Livs of Turaida and Koknese pass under the Order and the bishop in 1208-1210 in the livonian-brothers-of-the-sword dossier; those are not repeated here for lack of an opened page that names the bishop's share. Riga War (1297-1330) is not drawn: the Wikipedia page by that title was not found. Review eu-14-x (2026-10-31): the region {admin1: Riga, country: Latvia} resolved to the whole Riga planning region (30 municipalities, about 13,150 km2), not the city; replaced by a circle round the city (8 km for the city, 10 km where Daugavgriva is included). REVISION after review eu-14-x (2026-10-31): (1) 1201 gain of the Riga circle from livonians added, with a keyframe from 1201 (Livonians page), so the capital (1202) lies inside the shape. (2) The 1207 disc was moved north-east of the Daugava (70 km round 25.1E 57.25N, as the reviewer suggested) and Semigallia is subtracted from every shape: overlap with the semigallians shape is now nil (was 32 cells); the whole shape is about 17,700 km2 against the infobox 18,000. (3) The 1207 gain counterpart is 'nobody', not livonians or the Brothers: neither dossier files a 1207 loss and the pages name no donor; the reviewer offered the other two. Open: the disc still overlaps the Turaida/Idumeja circles of the livonians dossier (Livonian to 1206/1208) and the Order's Cliopatria-derived shapes in the Brothers dossier (eu-14-e), which should subtract the archbishopric from 1207. The Riga War (1297-1330) page failed again (Riga_War and Riga_War_(1297%E2%80%931330) both url_not_found); the archbishop's districts remain unnamed.
